artists.biography:
The Blues Brothers (or, more formally, The Blues Brothers’ Show Band and Revue) are an American blues and soul revivalist band founded in 1978 by comedy actors Dan Aykroyd and John Belushi as part of a musical sketch on Saturday Night Live. Belushi and Aykroyd, respectively in character as lead vocalist "Joliet Jake" Blues and harmonica player/backing vocalist Elwood Blues, fronted the band, which was composed of well-known and respected musicians. The band made its debut as the musical guest on the April 22, 1978, episode of Saturday Night Live.
The band began to take on a life beyond the confines of the television screen, releasing an album, Briefcase Full of Blues, in 1978, and then having a Hollywood film, The Blues Brothers, created around its characters in 1980.
After the death of Belushi in 1982, the Blues Brothers have continued to perform with a rotation of guest singers and other band members. The band reformed in 1988 for a world tour and again in 1998 for a sequel to the film, Blues Brothers 2000. They make regular appearances at musical festivals worldwide.
On August 31, 2011, it was announced that Dan Aykroyd and Judith Belushi Pisano were pitching a new Blues Brothers TV series to primetime networks.

perplexity.description:
Briefcase Full of Blues, released in 1978 on Atlantic Records (not Friday Music), is the debut album by The Blues Brothers. The album is a vibrant collection of blues and soul covers, drawing from the 1950s to the 1970s, and features energetic performances of songs originally made famous by artists such as Otis Redding, Sam & Dave, and King Floyd. Fronted by comedians John Belushi and Dan Aykroyd, the band is backed by a powerhouse group of seasoned session musicians, including Stax legends Steve Cropper and Donald “Duck” Dunn, which lends the album a genuine, rootsy authenticity. The musical style blends classic R&B, soul, and blues, with tight arrangements and spirited vocals that capture the essence of the genres.

As the first full-length release by The Blues Brothers, Briefcase Full of Blues established the group’s signature sound and set the stage for their subsequent work, including the iconic film adaptation. The album was recorded live at the Universal Amphitheater in Los Angeles, contributing to its dynamic, concert-like atmosphere. It was a commercial success, reaching No. 1 on the Billboard 200 and achieving double-platinum status. The singles “Soul Man” and “Rubber Biscuit” both charted in the Top 40, further cementing the album’s popularity. Critics praised the album for its energetic performances and respect for the source material, helping to introduce classic blues and soul to a new generation.
